subject: Clarify: prohibition on adaptive model training and cross-border subprocessor transfers
messages:
From: Leah Brown <leah.brown@medsolv.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MedSolv Procurement <procurement@medsolv.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on adaptive-training prohibition + subprocessor transfers

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. Before we progress procurement I need a couple of contractual clarifications so our legal and security teams can sign off:

1) Prohibition on adaptive training: Can Redwood commit that MedSolv customer content (prompts, documents, API inputs, and generated outputs) will not be used to further train or adapt any Redwood models or third-party models unless MedSolv provides explicit written permission? We need this stated plainly in the DPA.

2) "Aggregated telemetry" carveout: Your team mentioned you might use aggregated telemetry for quality improvements — please define what categories are included and confirm whether any such telemetry could ever be reversed to reconstruct customer prompts or outputs.

3) Subprocessor transfers and cross-border movement: Provide an up-to-date subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors are located outside the US/EU (we have EU residency needs). If transfers to other territories or downstream vendors are possible, we need the contractual commitment and an export control pathway (SFTP or API export).

4) Retention and provenance: How long are prompts and model outputs retained in logs or caches? Can we get an SFTP export of tenant data on request and proof of deletion after termination?

I attached a short statement of our concerns. Could you send a redline or proposed language this week? Procurement is targeting a March 31 signature if we can resolve these items.

Best,
Leah Brown
Director, Information Security
MedSolv Health

Attachment: medsolv_privacy_questions.docx (stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Brown <leah.brown@medsolv.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on adaptive-training prohibition + subprocessor transfers

Leah —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a proposed DPA redline and current subprocessor inventory for your team to review.

1) Adaptive training / no-derive commitment: Redwood can commit — for this agreement we propose the following contract clause in plain language: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to further train, fine-tune, or adapt any models (internal or third-party) without Customer's prior written consent." This applies to hosted API and dedicated/reserved tiers.

2) Aggregated telemetry: When we say "aggregated telemetry" we mean anonymized performance metrics (token latency percentiles, error-class counters, anonymous model failure rates) and non-content usage statistics. We will not use content-level logs (raw prompts or responses) for model training unless the customer explicitly opts in. We will add explicit definitions and retention windows in the DPA (suggested default: telemetry retention 90 days, content logs retention 30 days unless otherwise agreed).

3) Subprocessors and transfers: Attached is our current subprocessor list. We do use a small set of cloud storage and networking subprocessors in APAC for regional routing; for customers requiring EU residency we offer options to pin region and prevent cross-border transfer. Contractually we can: (a) commit not to transfer Customer Content to subprocessors outside agreed regions; (b) notify customers 30 days before adding a new subprocessor and provide a mechanism to object.

4) Retention/export: We support tenant-level exports (SFTP or secure API) and can provide a one-time data extract on termination. We also support customer-requested deletion with attestation. I included a draft of the clause that describes export/retention.

Actions I propose: Neha/legal to review the attached redline and confirm the precise retention windows and notification cadence. Priyom/product to confirm the technical export playbook and retention defaults. Marissa/CS to prepare an SFTP onboarding checklist for MedSolv.

I'll be available for a quick call tomorrow if your team wants to walk through the redlines.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_medsolv_v1.pdf (redline), redlined_subprocessors_list.csv (stub)

From: Leah Brown <leah.brown@medsolv.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MedSolv Procurement <procurement@medsolv.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on adaptive-training prohibition + subprocessor transfers

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick response and the attachments. Procurement and security reviewed the redline and they have three follow-ups:

• Aggregated telemetry definition: Please add a non-exhaustive list in the DPA of the fields considered telemetry vs content. We need explicit confirmation that request/response text, embeddings, and prompt metadata are not captured for training unless opted in.

• Retention windows: 30 days for content logs is acceptable only if you provide an explicit deletion attestation and make sure cached KV is ephemeral. Can you confirm whether ephemeral KV caches are flushed on tenant inactivity or termination? Specify maximum retention.

• "No derivatives" language: Procurement requests a clause that prevents Redwood from creating derivative works from Customer Content that could be offered elsewhere; i.e., no model artifacts or weights derived from MedSolv data.

We also need the SOC 2 audit schedule and a sample deletion attestation. If you can incorporate these items and resend an updated redline, procurement will move to term-sheet sign-off. Our target remains March 31 but delays if legal needs more time.

Thanks,
Leah Brown
Director, Information Security
MedSolv Health

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on adaptive-training prohibition + subprocessor transfers — MedSolv asks and next steps

Team —

Forwarding MedSolv's latest review. Summary and proposed owners below:

1) Define telemetry vs content (legal + product): Neha/Priyom — add a short non-exhaustive appendix listing telemetry fields (latency_ms, error_code, model_id, token_counts) and explicitly exclude request/response text, embeddings, prompt metadata from training pipelines unless customer opts in. Suggest retention defaults: telemetry 90d, content logs 30d (max) with explicit deletion attestation on request.

2) KV/cache behavior (product): Priyom — confirm eviction behavior for tenant KV and provide maximum retention guarantee; ensure ephemeral caches are flushed on termination.

3) No-derivatives clause (legal): Neha — draft explicit "no derivatives" language preventing Redwood from producing model artifacts or trained weights that derive from MedSolv Content.

4) SOC2 and attestation (CS/legal): Marissa — attach most recent SOC2 report and prepare a template deletion attestation; coordinate secure SFTP export playbook.

Milestone: we should return an updated redline by Tue 2027-03-22 to keep MedSolv on the March 31 procurement timeline. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/D-48291.

Attachments: previously sent DPA_redline_medsolv_v1.pdf, redlined_subprocessors_list.csv

Cheers,
Vivek
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
